;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[September 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***An explosion occurs in [[Zhari District]], [[Kandahar Province|Kandahar]], when a motorcycle hits a mine. One person is killed and another injured. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan/civilian-killed-kandahar-roadside-blast (Tolo News)]
***During clashes between the [[Taliban]] and security forces in [[Faryab Province|Faryab]], 22 militants are killed and 24 others are injured. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan/22-taliban-killed-faryab-clashes-mod (Tolo News)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Three [[Somali Armed Forces|Somali]] [[special forces]] officers are killed and one [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. officer]] seriously wounded when a [[car bomb]] explodes outside a special force base in an attack in the country's south, in a village some 60 km (around 40 miles) from the port city of [[Kismayo]]. [[Jihadist]] group [[al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] claims responsibility, saying it "killed U.S. personnel". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-security/three-somali-special-forces-killed-us-officer-wounded-in-car-bomb-somali-official-says-idUSKBN25Y147?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Arts and culture
*A [[shipwreck]] discovered in the [[Norwegian trench]] in April 2017 is confirmed to be that of the [[German cruiser Karlsruhe|German cruiser ''Karlsruhe'']], according to Norwegian power grid operator [[Statnett]] and a maritime archaeologist. The cruiser was sunk by a British [[Royal Navy]] submarine on April 9, 1940, during the opening stages of [[Operation Weserübung]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-norway-germany-ww2/sunken-german-world-war-two-warship-found-off-norway-idUKKBN25Y1R5 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[Argentine debt restructuring]]
**[[S&P Global Ratings]] upgrades Argentina's long term sovereign-credit rating to "CCC+" from "SD" citing the end of prolonged foreign and local law foreign currency debt restructurings, effectively pulling the country out of [[default (finance)|default]] territory after the country successfully restructured over [[United States dollar|$]]100 billion in sovereign debt. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-argentina-debt/sp-lifts-argentina-rating-out-of-default-after-debt-revamp-idUSKBN25Y1X1?il=0 (Reuters)] 

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Sudan floods]]
**[[Sudan]] declares a [[state of emergency]] after unprecedented [[flooding]] kills at least 99 people and leaves over 100,000 people homeless. The floods are the worst on record in Sudan since 1988, while the [[Nile]] has risen to its highest levels in a century. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/sep/05/sudan-declares-state-of-emergency-record-flooding (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2020 California wildfires]]
**The [[United States Forest Service]] announces that [[List of California state forests|forests]] in [[California]] will close after wildfires reach two million acres. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/wireStory/remote-towns-evacuated-california-wildfire-grows-72863443 (ABC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois]]
****The number of cases in [[Illinois]] exceeds 250,000. [https://chicago.suntimes.com/coronavirus/2020/9/7/21426172/illinois-coronavirus-covid-cases-monday-sept-7 (''The Chicago Sun-Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
****The [[Florida Department of Health]] reports 1,838 cases in 24 hours, the [[Florida|state]]'s lowest since June 15. [https://www.miamiherald.com/news/coronavirus/article245543900.html (''The Miami Herald'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] announces a deal with [[CSL Limited]] to secure access to the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] being developed by [[AstraZeneca]] and receive the first batches of the potential vaccine in January. [https://www.huffingtonpost.com.au/entry/australias-secures-access-to-astrazeneca-covid-19-vaccine-within-months_au_5f557a87c5b6946f3eb3cb1e (''HuffPost'')] [http://www.straitstimes.com/asia/australianz/australias-csl-agrees-to-manufacture-two-covid-19-vaccine-candidates (''The Straits Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
***[[India]] surpasses [[Brazil]] as the country with the second-most cases in the world, behind the [[United States]]. India reported 90,802 cases in the past 24 hours and 1,016 deaths, recording the single largest increase of cases in the world in almost a month. [https://apnews.com/f926306025e5e28f69b6ef6207f7d0c7 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
***[[Spain]] becomes the first [[Western Europe]]an and [[European Union]] country to surpass 500,000 cases. [https://www.abc.es/sociedad/abci-espana-primer-pais-europeo-superar-500000-casos-sumar-26500-tras-semana-202009071921_noticia.html (ABC.es)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2020/sep/07/coronavirus-live-news-cases-rising-in-22-us-states-as-france-declares-more-covid-19-red-zones (''The Guardian'')]

;International relations
*[[India–Russia relations]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
**[[Russia]] says that they will begin phase 3 clinical trials of their [[Gam-COVID-Vac]] vaccine in India later this month. [https://www.india.com/news/world/sputnik-v-russia-plans-to-begin-phase-3-trial-of-corona-vaccine-in-india-this-month-results-likely-by-nov-end-4134639/ (India.com)]
*Aftermath of the [[2020 Malian coup d'état]]
**At a summit in [[Niamey]], [[Niger]], regional bloc [[ECOWAS]] gives the [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian military]] rulers a deadline of September 15 to appoint a new civilian [[President of Mali|President]] and [[Prime Minister of Mali|Prime Minister]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/09/africa-leaders-mali-military-gov-president-sep-15-200907183944798.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**Prominent [[Belarusian democracy movement|opposition]] figure and activist [[Maria Kalesnikava]] is taken away by masked men in [[Minsk]] and bundled into a van. [[Ministry of Internal Affairs (Belarus)|Police]] say that they did not detain her. [https://www.dw.com/en/belarus-opposition-figure-maria-kolesnikova-detained-by-masked-men/a-54840475 (DW)]
*[[Killing of Jennifer Laude]]
**[[President of the Philippines|Philippine President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] [[pardon]] [[United States Marine]] Joseph Scott Pemberton for the killing of a [[transgender woman]] in 2015. [[human rights in the Philippines|Human rights]] activists condemn the decision while Duterte defends his move saying Pemberton was treated "unfairly". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-philippines-usa-transgender/philippine-president-pardons-u-s-marine-jailed-for-transgender-killing-idUSKBN25Y1D6?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Assassination of Jamal Khashoggi]]
**[[government of Saudi Arabia|Saudi Arabia]] issues final convictions for eight people for the [[murder]] of [[Jamal Khashoggi]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/saudi-arabian-court-issues-final-verdict-8-people-death-journalist-n1239468 (NBC News)]
*[[Istanbul nightclub shooting]]
**A [[government of Turkey|Turkish]] court sentences [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] militant Abdulkadir Masharipov to [[life imprisonment]], plus an additional 1,368 years in prison, for killing 39 people and injuring 79 more at an [[Istanbul]] nightclub in 2017. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-security-reina/turkish-court-sentences-nightclub-shooting-suspect-to-life-in-jail-idUSKBN25Y1RN?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[One-China policy]], [[Politics of Solomon Islands]]
**The [[government of Solomon Islands]] says that a proposed [[independence referendum]] in [[Malaita Province]] is illegal. Daniel Suidani, the provincial premier of Malaita, proposed the referendum in protest to the decision by the central government to switch recognition from [[Taiwan]] to [[China]] last year. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/425464/solomons-govt-says-malaita-independence-referendum-illegal (RNZ)]
